about: Street words for the voice, the on-screen text and the post text (the owner, 2026-10-06: films should sound like the street, mild Georgian folk insults are fine and get shared; the heaviest words make the brand ugly). "allowed": mild folk words a film may use, 1 to 3 per film, mixed, only in a persona ("me") line or a made-up dialogue, never put in a real person's mouth (no invented quote, no vulgar word about a named person). "banned": never, in any form (the check matches a word that STARTS with one of these stems, so ordinary words that merely contain the letters pass; mother insults are judged by the brief, because a stem list cannot tell „დედაშენი რეკავს“ from an insult). "rotation": a word used in the last film is not used again in the next one (tools/ci/streetwords.mjs reads the ledger). Group slurs (orientation, ethnicity, religion, a disability used as an insult), mother insults and sexual content are out whatever the list says. Russian loanwords stay out (CLAUDE.md rule 4, no Russianisms: ლოშარა, ჩმო, ტრუსი, ფრაერი were left off on purpose).
